payload.title: @FrickQuery object-collection SwiftUI property wrapper
payload.description:
## Frick today
The SwiftUI layer (packages/swift/Sources/FrickSwift/SwiftUI/FrickStream.swift) ships @FrickStream and @FrickPresence — but read their bodies: they bind to event-log tails and presence rows, NOT object collections. There is no object-query property wrapper. This is a NEW capability for Frick, not just dedup.

## What RangerCRM built (port source of truth)
/Users/bri/dev/RangerCRM/RangerCRM/Model/RangerData/Services/FrickQuery.swift — a genuine @FetchRequest drop-in:
- @FrickQuery property wrapper resolving a typed array and exposing FrickQueryResults<Item>
- FrickQueryResults conforms to RandomAccessCollection (ForEach/subscript work out of the box), with write-through `sortDescriptors` and `filter`
- projectedValue: a Binding into the sort descriptors so sort-picker UIs mutate them via `$`
- FrickSort<Item>: value-type keyPath comparator (String/Date/Double/Int overloads), replacing SortDescriptor<NSManagedObject>
This is the piece that let RangerCRM view code mechanically swap off @FetchRequest with a one-line declaration change.

## What the port gives us
Completes the SwiftUI trio: @FrickStream (events) + @FrickPresence (presence) + @FrickQuery (objects). Any future Frick app gets declarative, sorted, filtered, live object lists for free.

## Coupling to resolve
RangerCRM's version resolves via `KeyPath<DataController, [Item]>` (app-specific) and reads DataController.shared. The port must re-anchor on the generic store registry (see that story) instead of an app DataController. RangerObject (the AnyObject marker the wrapper is generic over, /Users/bri/dev/RangerCRM/RangerCRM/Model/RangerData/Services/RangerObject.swift) folds into the FrickModel protocol.

Blocked by: store registry (needs a generic anchor).
